headline: Alivus Life Sciences Limited announces acquisition via board meeting outcome
sum: Alivus Life Sciences Limited disclosed a board-approved acquisition via Regulation 30 intimation to NSE and BSE on 18 August 2026; specific target, valuation and structure not disclosed in the outcome filing.
implication: The Regulation 30 disclosure regime requires listed entities to announce material acquisitions immediately post-board approval, triggering standstill and pricing transparency duties; the bare intimation signals either a confidentiality period (vendor lock-in) or Phase 1 of a two-stage disclosure process.
detail: Alivus Life Sciences Limited, a listed pharmaceutical company, notified both NSE and BSE of a board resolution approving an acquisition under SEBI (LODR) Regulation 30. The outcome filing provides no detail on target identity, purchase price, asset class, or closing conditions-standard for early-stage M&A announcements under Indian disclosure norms, which permit staged disclosure once material terms crystallise. The transaction likely triggered mandatory review under the SEBI takeover code (if the target is listed) or CCI merger thresholds (if combined turnover or assets exceed ₹1,000 crore), pending release of full particulars.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations & Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Regulation 30
framework.note: Central | Mandatory immediate disclosure of board-approved acquisitions to stock exchanges; sets materiality threshold and timelines for material corporate actions.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares & Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Sections 4, 5 & 6
framework.note: Central | If target is listed entity or acquisition triggers 25%+ shareholding, mandatory open offer, escrow & pricing norms apply; review required once target is named.

Central | If combined turnover or assets of acquirer + target exceed ₹1,000 crore, CCI merger notification and approval required before completion; exemptions for greenfield/acquisition of shares only.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FMEA), 1999 & Rules (if cross-border)
framework.note: Conditional | If target is foreign entity or acquisition funded by foreign investment, RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme or FDI Schedule approval may apply.
Sector-specific | Transfer of manufacturing licences, brand approvals and regulatory clearances post-acquisition require MeitY/CDSCO sign-off; post-close integration plan must map licence migrations.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Sections 180(1)(a) & 394, read with Company Board Rules
framework.note: Central | Board approval for acquisition (per Section 180) and shareholder ratification (if material per Section 394) are statutory prerequisites; all board minutes and related-party disclosures must be on record.

Conditional | If structured as merger/amalgamation under Section 2(1B), tax-neutral scheme of arrangement under Section 47 may apply; slippage to taxable acquisition triggers capital gains & withholding on consideration.

Central | Board approval and public disclosure trigger trading blackout windows; Alivus insiders (board, KMPs, designated persons) face restricted dealing until 48 hrs post-disclosure under the Regulation 30 safe harbour.

conditions: CCI merger clearance (if combined enterprise value or turnover > ₹1,000 crore)
SEBI open offer obligations (if target is listed or acquisition triggers 25%+ shareholding under Takeovers Regulations)
Regulatory approvals from CDSCO/MeitY (if target holds pharmaceutical manufacturing or import licences)
Shareholder approval via postal ballot or general meeting (if material per Section 394, Companies Act)
structure.novel: Early-stage Regulation 30 intimation with no pricing or target detail; suggests either confidentiality/standstill clause in LOI or staged disclosure pending CCI/SEBI gating (common in pharma M&A where regulatory approvals precede public terms).

triggers.note: Immediate disclosure obligation on board approval; creates 48-hour trading blackout and establishes safe harbour for related-party involvement in execution.
If combined turnover or assets exceed ₹1,000 crore, pre-completion CCI notification and approval mandatory; deal closure conditioned on CCI clearance letter.
If acquisition results in 25%+ shareholding of listed target (or unlisted but meets public interest test), open offer framework and pricing formula apply.
Transfer of manufacturing authorisations, brand approvals and regulatory clearances from target to acquirer post-close; CDSCO approval timeline typically 30–90 days post-close.

firms.note: No law firm or counsel disclosed in the Regulation 30 outcome filing; counsel names typically appear in subsequent detailed disclosure or press release.
